newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - July 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - July 10.

DAILY TELEGRAPH-- BURTON TO REVIEW SHARE OPTIONS

Retailer Burton Group is to examine share option packages for executive directors following the announcement of plans this week to demerge the group's Debenhams department store chain. Debenhams will become a separately-quoted public company next year. John Hoerner, current chief executive at Burton Group, could make a profit of more than three million stg if he was able to exercise his share options immediately.
-- ALLIED PLANS 4,000 JOBS

Allied Domecq, the drinks and pubs group, has announced plans to spend 150m stg on expanding and upgrading its retail estate. The move is expected to create up to 4,000 full and part-time jobs at the group's three pub brands - Big Steak, Firkin and Mr Q. The family-oriented Big Steak group will have another 43 outlets added to its existing 248 sites.
-- ANOTHER DIRECTOR QUITS C&W

Allen Saunders, formerly an executive director in charge of corporate communications at Nynex CableComms, has joined the growing number of directors departing Cable & Wireless Communications, the cable TV and telephone company formed by the merger of Cable & Wireless's Mercury with Nynex and two other cable companies. The move comes as C&WC announced that Roy Payne, director of the Cable Communications Association, has been appointed to the top corporate communications post at the group.
THE TIMES
-- LIDDELL MAKES NEW ATTACK ON PENSION FIRMS

Helen Liddell, Economic Secretary to the Treasury, has criticised 24 leading firms in the pensions industry over the issue of misselling of personal pensions. Liddell blasted the firms for their poor performance in compensating victims of misselling. After 'naming and shaming' some of the worst offenders last month, Liddell intends to publish progress figures every month and said she will decide on whether further sanctions are needed in the autumn.
-- DIXONS SALES SOAR 17 PER CENT ON BACK OF WINDFALL PAYOUTS

High Street electrical goods retailer Dixons has reported a 17 per cent leap in like-for-like sales in the first nine weeks of this year as consumers rush to cash in their windfall payments. Over half the increase has been attributed to people spending windfall money, with sales focused on more expensive items such as PCs and TVs. Pre-tax profits rose from 135.2m stg to 190.2m stg for the 53 weeks to May 3.
-- SAINSBURY'S SHARES AND SALES BOUNCE BACK

Supermarket chain J Sainsbury has reported an increase of 4.2 per cent in underlying sales growth for the first quarter. The news boosted the price of shares in the company, which lost 12 per cent of their value after a profits warning in January. In trading Wednesday, they gained 11.5p to close at 399.5p, just short of their 1997 high.
THE GUARDIAN
-- CO-OP SNEERS AT CAPITALIST RIVALS

The Co-op Bank, whick markets itself on its ethical business practice, has reported that its customers are sick of the increasing profit focus among most British companies. The claim was based on the results of a survey of the Bank's million-plus customers on their attitude to its partnership approach, which attempts to balance the needs of customers, staff and five other stakeholder groups.
-- GREMLINS IN MILLENNIUM MACHINE LIE IN WAIT FOR EURO

Robin Guenier, the head of the British government's Taskforce 2000 project to ensure that computer systems are ready to cope with the date change to the Millennium, has warned that the introduction of a single European currency will be a disaster unless it is delayed by at least two years. He claims that companies should be allowed time to prepare their systems for the date change.
-- BRITISH BIO INVESTORS SWALLOW BITTER PILL AS 'WONDER DRUGS' ARE DELAYED

British Biotechnology, the former darling of the Stock Exchange, saw more than 100m stg wiped off its value after the company reported a loss of almost 30m stg. Investors were dismayed by news of clinical trials of two of the biotechnology company's most promising drugs - the cancer treatment Marimastat, and Zacutex, a treatment for acute pancreatitis.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- COAL COMPENSATION BILL MAY HIT 1.3 BILLION STG

Accounts published Wednesday by British Coal warn that the cost of compensating former mine workers for personal injury and industrial diseases could be 'very significant', with some reports suggesting it could exceed the 1.3bn stg raised through the privatisation of the company. British Coal said it has been unable to make a special provision in its accounts for potential compensation because of the 'considerable uncertainty' over its liability and the size of any damages.
-- LOW & BONAR ENDS KELLOGG CONTRACT

Low & Bonar is to terminate a contract to supply cartons to cereal maker Kellogg, claiming it was unable to meet the new low price required to retain the contract for a further five years when the agreement expired in May 2000. The Kellogg contract is worth about 40m stg a year to Low, which represents almost 10 per cent of group turnover.
-- UNITED DRUG BUYS DUBLIN FOR IR15M POUNDS

United Drug has moved to expand its wholesale business in Ireland with an agreed IR15.1m pounds bid for Dublin Drug, a wholesaler and distributor of pharmaceutical and healthcare products in Ireland. United will offer three of its shares for every four in Dublin, and the offer includes an additional payment of 10p per Dublin share after two years subject to 75 per cent of the business transferring to United.
